title: Decipher
text:
{{Hatnote|For the 1995–2001 printed game period, see [[Decipher era]].}} '''Decipher, Inc.''' (often just '''Decipher''') was the Norfolk, Virginia game company that published the printed ''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game (SWCCG) from December 1995 through 2001.[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. Decipher, Inc.], Wikipedia[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia [[File:Decipher logo 1999.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Decipher logo, 1999. Source: LOTR-TCG wiki.]] == Founder / leadership == [[Warren Holland]] founded Decipher in '''1983''' and was its Chairman and CEO. The company was headquartered in downtown Norfolk, Virginia.[https://web.archive.org/web/20000815233727/http://www.decipher.com/aboutdecipher/index.html About Decipher], Decipher.com (Internet Archive, 15 August 2000)[https://web.archive.org/web/20000815233727/http://www.decipher.com/aboutdecipher/findus/ Find Us], Decipher.com (Internet Archive, 15 August 2000) == Early years (puzzles and party games) == Decipher began in 1983 with contest jigsaw puzzles. It then built a long-running party-game line around ''How to Host a Murder'', and later marketed ''Pente'' under a license acquired from Parker Brothers.[https://web.archive.org/web/20000815233727/http://www.decipher.com/aboutdecipher/vision/ Vision], Decipher.com (Internet Archive, 15 August 2000) — company statement signed Warren Holland, Chairman and CEO, citing inception in 1983 The company's slogan of the CCG era was '''Decipher: The Art of Great Games'''.[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Decipher Decipher], Wookieepedia[https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Decipher], LOTR-TCG Wiki == CCG era (overview) == After ''Magic: The Gathering'' popularized collectible card games, designers [[Tom Braunlich]] and [[Rollie Tesh]] pitched a media-licensed CCG approach. Decipher's first major CCG was the [[Star Trek CCG|''Star Trek: The Next Generation'' CCG]] (1994), followed by SWCCG (1995). Later titles included ''Austin Powers'', ''Young Jedi'', ''Jedi Knights'', ''The Lord of the Rings'' TCG, several youth-market licenses (''.hack'', ''Beyblade'', ''Mega Man''), the original-IP ''WARS'' TCG, and finally ''Fight Klub''. At peak, Star Wars CCG sales were among the top non-''Magic'' CCGs. == SWCCG == Decipher released SWCCG under a Lucasfilm license. Its designers were [[Tom Braunlich]], [[Rollie Tesh]], [[Jerry Darcy]] and [[Warren Holland]] (see [[Creators of SWCCG]]). Printed Decipher sets begin with [[Premiere Limited]] (December 1995); the full Decipher expansion list is on the [[Main Page]]. == After the license == ''Main articles: [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]], [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]]'' Decipher lost the ''Star Wars'' license when its contract was not renewed; the license ended in December 2001. Company leadership publicly supported a Players' Committee and advocate structure so organized play and later virtual cards could continue.[[History of the Players Committee]] After 2001 the game's stewardship passed to the community and the [[Players Committee]]. == Decline == Decipher contracted over several years after license losses and underperforming launches. FanHQ and fan-club magazine efforts faded as social media grew. ''WARS'' and several youth CCGs struggled, RPG lines were cut, and staff reductions delayed late sets for its remaining licensed games. Physical product ended after ''Fight Klub'' (c. 2008), while decipher.com posted intermittent "coming back" messages for years afterward. === Embezzlement === Former Decipher finance executive '''Rick Eddleman''', Holland's brother-in-law, pleaded guilty to embezzling more than US$1.5 million from the company.[https://web.archive.org/web/20090316043101/http://hamptonroads.com/node/501025 Norfolk man pleads guilty to embezzling more than $1.5m], ''The Virginian-Pilot'' (Internet Archive) In 2009 he was sentenced to about six years in prison.[https://web.archive.org/web/20121002195010/http://hamptonroads.com/2009/07/game-company-embezzler-gets-6-years-must-repay-910000 Game company embezzlement was betrayal to family], ''The Virginian-Pilot'' (Internet Archive) A civil settlement came to about US$8.9 million. According to documents Holland posted online, losses over Eddleman's 1990s–2001 tenure were about US$9 million.[https://web.archive.org/web/20091005031807/http://www.embezzlementfromdecipher.com/ EmbezzlementFromDecipher.com], archived overview hosted by Holland (Internet Archive) == Logos == Decipher used several corporate logos and wordmarks. File:Decipher logo 1999.jpg|1999 logo. Source: [https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/File:decipher_old_logo.jpg LOTR-TCG wiki] File:Decipher logo wordmark.png|Condensed wordmark. Source: [https://memory-alpha.fandom.com/wiki/File:Decipher_logo.png Memory Alpha] File:Decipher logo wordmark gradient.jpg|Web header wordmark. Source: [https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/File:RFD-logo.jpg LOTR-TCG wiki] == Japanese-language releases == [[Takara]] partnered with Decipher to develop and distribute Japanese-language Star Wars CCG products.[https://groups.google.com/g/rec.arts.sf.starwars.games/c/2ZwVPTmzOUs Rich Loftus, Star Wars CCG in Japan], Decipher (1 April 1997), reposted on rec.arts.sf.starwars.games (3 April 1997). == See also == * [[Warren Holland]] · [[Creators of SWCCG]] * [[Star Wars CCG]] · [[Star Trek CCG]] * [[Decipher.com]] · [[Decipher mailing lists]] * [[Decipher and the Star Wars CCG Lucasfilm license]] · [[Decipher after the Star Wars license]] * [[History of the Players Committee]] · [[Players Committee]] · [[Players Committee-Lucasfilm agreement]] * [[Decipher era]] * [[Main Page]] (Decipher expansion tiles) * Sister encyclopedias: [https://wiki.lotrtcgpc.net/wiki/Decipher Decipher (LOTR-TCG wiki)] · [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decipher,_Inc. title: Takara
text:
[[File:Takara-company-logo.png|thumb|right|Takara logo]]
'''Takara''' was a Japanese toy company and [[Decipher]]'s partner for the Japanese-language [[Star Wars CCG]]. Takara developed and distributed Japanese versions of the game, including three expansions and two introductory two-player products.<ref name="loftus">[https://groups.google.com/g/rec.arts.sf.starwars.games/c/2ZwVPTmzOUs Rich Loftus, Star Wars CCG in Japan], Decipher (1 April 1997), reposted on rec.arts.sf.starwars.games (3 April 1997).</ref><ref name="encyclopedia">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 41–45. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== Partnership with Decipher ==
Decipher and Takara announced their partnership in December 1996 to develop and distribute a Japanese-language edition. In 1997, Decipher executive Steve Stanley described Takara as Decipher's marketing partner and sole distributor in Japan. Takara demonstrated the game at the Tokyo Toy Show in March 1997 and was translating the tournament kit. At the time, Takara could not ship Japanese Premiere outside Japan; Decipher was investigating ways to make the cards available elsewhere.<ref name="loftus" />

Former Players Committee advocate [[Jim Colson]] wrote that Decipher supplied card templates and artwork to Takara, which translated and printed the Japanese cards. Colson reported that some Japanese players encountered translation differences and came to prefer English cards. He attributed declining demand for Japanese printings to this preference; his account does not establish the date or terms on which the Takara–Decipher arrangement ended.<ref name="colson">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=8359 Post your questions here!], Jim Colson, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums (25 July 2009).</ref>

<ref name="encyclopedia" />

Japanese Premiere starter sets included a Japanese rulebook, and Takara issued player's guides. The two-player games included Japanese rules materials; the Empire Strikes Back game also included a sample-game booklet.<ref name="encyclopedia" />

== Later Japanese cards ==
Decipher included Japanese-language cards among the reprints in [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]]. Its announcement also identified [[Darth Vader (Japanese Reflections II Foil)|Japanese Darth Vader]] as a foil case topper.<ref name="ref2">[https://theforce.net/ccg/story/Star_Wars_Reflections_II_Official_Announcement_74652.asp Star Wars: Reflections II Official Announcement], Decipher announcement reproduced by TheForce.Net (6 November 2000).</ref> Colson wrote that Decipher purchased the Japanese product from its Japanese distributor, including the nonfoil Japanese cards used in Reflections packs.<ref name="colson-import">[https://forum.starwarsccg.org/viewtopic.php?t=71003 Collecting archive items], Jim Colson, Star Wars CCG Players Committee Forums.</ref>

Japanese foil cards also appeared in [[Reflections III: A Collector's Bounty]], including Luke Skywalker and The Circle Is Now Complete from Japanese Premiere.<ref name="cardlist">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Star Wars CCG Complete Card List 4.0], Reflections III foil list. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009184033/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Internet Archive].</ref>

== Other planned language releases ==
The planned [[Cancelled German release of SWCCG|German release]] involved a company identified as Queens Games and was not completed. A Spanish-language release also did not appear. See [[Translations of SWCCG]] for their surviving materials and publication history.

== Company history ==
Takara's predecessor, Sato Vinyl Industry, was founded by Yasuta Sato in 1955.<ref name="founder">[https://www.takaratomy.co.jp/ir/financial/pdf_takara/businessreport/05_jigyou.pdf Takara 50-year history], Takara.</ref> Takara's products included Licca-chan dolls and Transformers toys. Keita Sato was president from 2000 to 2005. In 2006, Takara merged with Tomy to form Takara Tomy.<ref name="history">[https://www.takaratomy.co.jp/company/history.html Company history], Takara Tomy. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20150424004951/http://www.takaratomy.co.jp:80/company/history.html Internet Archive].</ref><ref name="keita">[https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2005/01/28/business/takara-chief-to-leave-over-fiscal-decline/ Takara chief to leave over fiscal decline], The Japan Times (28 January 2005).</ref><ref name="merger">[https://www.takaratomy.co.jp/english/ir/etc/faq.html Investor relations FAQ], Takara Tomy. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20111120003649/http://www.takaratomy.co.jp:80/english/ir/etc/faq.html Internet Archive].</ref>

text:

Causes massive disruptions in weapon, engine and computer systems aboard a target. Disables starship defenses against tractor beams. |game_text=Use 2 Force to deploy on your Star Destroyer. May target a starship using 1 Force. Draw destiny. If destiny +2 > defense value, all starship weapons deployed on target are lost, armor or maneuver = 0 and hyperspeed = 0. |printings='''Decipher''' — [[Ion Cannon]] (1_318o)
'''Decipher Errata''' — '''this page''' (1_318)
'''Decipher (Japanese)''' — [[Ion Cannon (Japanese)]] |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (Ion Cannon; November 1998) * Printed face: [[Ion Cannon]] |strategy=By Brian Leehttps://web.archive.org/web/20020804011354/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/ioncannon.html A great combo to do with the "[[Ion Cannon]]" and the "[[Turbolaser Battery]]" is to fire the "[[Ion Cannon]]" (preferably at a "Correlian Corvette" filled with passengers) at a capital Starship. Then, if you hit them, fire your "[[Turbolaser Battery]]" at the ship. It's near impossible to miss the ship considering it has an armor of 0. If you do this all in one turn the Light side can't do anything about it, which really could be nice if the starship is filled with troublesome characters like [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]], etc. |rulings=* Whether fired during battle or at another time, the target starship is armor/maneuver and hyperspeed = 0 until it leaves play (or until something makes it 'restored to normal'). * Weapons aboard the starship are only lost as a one-time response to the Cannon firing. Weapons can subsequently be deployed on the starship without becoming lost. |combos=* [[Ion Cannon]] + [[Turbolaser Battery]][https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Ion%20Cannon Scomp: Ion Cannon]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020174249/https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json Internet Archive] * [[Ion Cannon]] + [[I Want That Ship]] * [[Ion Cannon]] + [[Tractor Beam]] |pulled_by=* [[I Can't Shake Him!]] |canceled_by=* [[Fire Extinguisher]] |characteristics=* cannon * ion cannon |has_refs=1 |notes=* Decipher [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998) revised game text. If you do this all in one turn the Light side can't do anything about it, which really could be nice if the starship is filled with troublesome characters like [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi{{!}}Obi-Wan]], etc. |reviews=* [[Jeff Hansen]], "Ion Cannon", Neglected Card Series, [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] (2000). Hansen calls it a Star Destroyer toy that strips a starship's weapons and defense value and strands it for a tractor beam or a beatdown. "This makes it easy prey for a tractor beam, and gets rid of obnoxious weapons to boot!"[http://www.geocities.com/CollegePark/Plaza/9433/articles/neglected28.html "Ion Cannon" review], Jeff Hansen, Neglected Card Series, Corellian Engineering Corporation fan site (GeoCities).
